topic: Euclid Telescope Discovers the Universe's Oldest 'Impossible' Quasar
angle: ESA's dark matter telescope just shattered the cosmic distance record by finding a supermassive black hole quasar 40 million years earlier than anything known, presenting astronomers with a monster that shouldn't have had enough time to grow.

facts: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar ever detected.
This new observation breaks the previous cosmic record by roughly 40 million years, peering deeper into the universe's infancy than ever before.
A quasar is an intensely bright galactic core powered by a supermassive black hole ravenously devouring surrounding gas and matter.
As matter swirls into the black hole's accretion disk at near-light speed, friction and gravity generate light that outshines hundreds of billions of stars combined.
Euclid was primarily designed to map dark matter and dark energy, making this ultra-ancient quasar detection an unexpected and serendipitous triumph.
The light detected by Euclid began its journey over 13 billion years ago, during the epoch known as cosmic dawn.
Finding a fully formed supermassive black hole this early in cosmic history defies conventional models of black hole growth.
Standard theories dictate that black holes start as stellar remnants and take billions of years of steady accretion and mergers to reach supermassive scale.
Astronomers hypothesize these early behemoths may have bypassed standard stellar lifecycles through 'direct collapse,' where giant primordial gas clouds fell straight into giant black holes.
Euclid's wide-angle infrared optics allowed it to scan vast patches of the sky to catch this rare cosmic relic that narrow-focus telescopes previously missed.
Astronomers have identified the farthest known quasar in existence.
The discovered quasar is recognized as the most ancient one observed in the universe.
Energy for this quasar is generated by a supermassive black hole.
The giant black hole dates back to approximately 630 million years following the Big Bang.
The object is described as the earliest monster black hole found in cosmic history.
The finding was reported by science media outlets including Space and Live Science.
The discovery is credited to the Euclid telescope, which located what is labeled an 'impossible' quasar.
